title: R-7: reliability, degraded states and provable owner-data backup
description: R-7 is the last step of the rollout: the reliability work that has to be true before Jacob would call Kitty shipped, bounded to gaps verified on main (2026-09-17, 7dd703c7) rather than to polish in general. docs/packets/OK-RC-01.md is prior art and is not activated here. The independent acceptance pass is deliberately not authored as a packet: the exact-candidate operator path already exists and is tested (`kitty accept` over gateway/mission_accept_cli.py and mission_runtime's running-product identity gates, 23 tests), the merge-time product-acceptance gate is scripts/pr_policy.py template validation, and the remaining PR-level automation is issue #349, which changes what the merge gate trusts and is Jacob's decision, not a bounded Builder packet. The three packets below close the verified reliability gaps: the health surface reports an unreadable schedule list as available with a count nobody measured; owner-data backup exists and is tested but is unreachable without a terminal; and the backup proof drill documents an invocation that does not run while drilling the legacy path the product does not use. Restore stays behind the existing CLI guard on purpose; it mutates live data and needs an interactive confirmation surface that does not exist yet. Every gate is a Python gate that runs in a Builder worktree today; no Node tooling appears in validation_commands because builder-frontend-proof-v1 has not landed. Packets run in sequence because they share the tests directory. Companion docs: docs/packets/R7-00.md, docs/packets/R7-01.md and docs/packets/R7-02.md.

packets.title: The health surface stops hiding a broken scheduler read
packets.objective: Make the cron health domain report a failed schedule read as degraded with a reason that names the failure, instead of leaving the supervisor's available status in place with a schedule count of zero that was never measured. This packet edits existing files only and creates no new production files.
acceptance_criteria: when the schedule list cannot be read, the cron domain reports degraded with a reason naming the read failure, asserted by a test that makes the read raise
a failed schedule read never reports a schedule count, asserted by the domain's detail carrying no measured-looking zero
when the schedule list reads successfully, the cron domain keeps the supervisor's status and the measured count, asserted by a test with a fixed schedule list
a failed schedule read does not raise out of the health surface
the existing health surface tests pass unchanged

packets.title: Owner data can be backed up and verified from the product
packets.objective: Add owner-data backup routes so Kitty can create, list and verify a backup without a terminal, reusing the existing backup implementation and refusing with a plain reason when there is nothing to protect. Restore is deliberately not part of this packet.
acceptance_criteria: a backup created through the gateway appears in the archive list with its creation time and copied file count read from its manifest
a backup request with no canonical personal database is refused with a plain-language reason and publishes nothing
verifying an intact archive restores it into a scratch directory, passes SQLite integrity_check and reports success, and verifying a damaged archive reports failure with a reason
an archive id that is not present in the archive list is rejected with a 404 before it can be used to build a filesystem path
the existing backup tests pass unchanged
a refused or failed backup request returns one plain sentence as its primary message; no stack trace, port, environment variable name or absolute file path is the text a person reads
a verify result says pass only after the named archive was actually restored and its SQLite files passed integrity check

packets.title: The backup proof drill runs as documented and proves the path the product uses
packets.objective: Make scripts/kitty_backup_proof.py run under its documented invocation and make its drill exercise the owner-data create and restore path that the ./kitty backup command uses, so its PASS verdict is evidence for the path the product actually writes. This packet edits existing files only and creates no new production files.
acceptance_criteria: the script runs successfully under the invocation its own docstring documents and prints the owner-data mode it proved, asserted by the packet's gate
the drill compares the pre-backup replica with the restored replica byte-for-byte and reports every mismatch
the drill still runs entirely inside a temp directory and never reads or writes the live data root
a restore with a mismatch still exits 1 with every difference printed
